comments.value: This can and would get so abused where artists just ban people they don't like. Its hard to gather in VRChat as it is, we don't need a bunch of clubhouses to form.
@{5c540514d859d512a8d1d2f9|full_name}: I want to remove someone from my world that I hate tho.
@{5c021357a58d0a7e70c3e515|full_name}: Exact reason why it should not be a thing.

The way to handle overly toxic players is to report them to VRChat, not to have per-world banning.
If someone is really bad enough that they need to be on a blacklist for your world, they're bad enough to be banned from VRChat as a whole and you should just report them. If they're not so bad that the moderation team would see them as a problem, then you probably just dislike them personally and that's not really a good enough reason to ban people from your public world. That could easily turn into a situation where the creators of the most popular worlds in VRChat become akin to game moderators, and that would get out of control quick.
A better idea if you really want to create a private world that only people you like can access would be a whitelisting system for private worlds. So people could create private club worlds that only members can join, if they want. I don't fault the idea as much if it's a private world to begin with. Though I really don't want VRChat to turn into a subreddit-style platform where everyone just condenses into their little bubbles, it's bad enough in that way as it is really. Newcomers to the game are feeling alienated enough already.
But public worlds are public. If you don't want the general populace using your world, it has no business being public.
This is a terrible idea I don't see going through. Anyone who gets behind this doesn't understand the term "public."

@{5eae36318b39a05c07a0d6cd|full_name}: Then it will be up to the Creator of the world to know how to balance things in order to let the community enjoy the world without even thinking about personal conflict.

@{5adfcb2a44b24b6ef7cb11ec|full_name}: The idea is in no way related to the Term "Public". It only intervenes only to the world creator to allow the Public to fully enjoy the VRChat experience, without any crossover from Client users or toxic players.

@{5eb6ff4435be1c7f156530a0|full_name}: "Public" is relevant in the sense of allowing anyone to experience the world. You are asking for a blacklist on top of this. It's essentially "I want people to experience my world EXCEPT these people because I think they're bad." If having toxic people in your world is such a problem to you then don't make it so they can join in the form of not making the world public for anyone to join. Making something Public and then gatekeeping it isn't what should happen here.

details:
The creators of the dream world. 
The creators could have the right to ban players from their world and add permissions to trusted players so they can moderate the world in case the creator is absent.
Why do this? 
It's simple, it will limit the "Toxic" players to be able to disturb the community that wants to play quietly.
title: Add Ban and Permission
